what.text: This page follows people displaced inside the Central African Republic by conflict and violence, counted by IDMC and by UNHCR and shown side by side.
At the end of 2025 both sources give the same figure, 427479 people.
Refugees from the country live mainly in Cameroon, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Chad.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of the Central African Republic in several periods since 2006.
From 2009 to 2014 the groups fighting the government include the CPJP, Seleka and anti-Balaka; from 2017 to 2025 they include anti-Balaka, the UPC and the CPC.
Floods and storms are the disasters recorded for the country in IDMC's data.

when.text: IDMC's figure peaked at 935000 in 2013, the year with the most new displacements from conflict, and fell to 411785 by 2016.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2013 and 2017 to 2024.

how.text: UNHCR's and IDMC's figures overlap and are counted differently, so they are shown side by side and never added.
IDMC's new displacements count movements, not people: someone forced to move twice in a year is counted twice.
The sources don't say where inside the country people moved to.
